title: Spawn-time slash-command resolution returns the raw prompt when cwd is the project root
outcome:
Observed 2026-09-26 by Termal::Opus (session-7304), while running /review-changes for the combined card/wait changeset.

termal_spawn_session with prompt '/review-code' and mode reviewer:
- cwd C:\github\Personal\TermAl\.tmp\wt-waits (a worktree inside the project), earlier the same day: resolved. Delegation delegation-4c2cea43-5939-4460-820a-32a8f14e2369 carried the full body of .claude/commands/review-code.md as its prompt.
- no cwd (defaults to the project root): NOT resolved. Delegation delegation-4c69b9d2-09cf-48dd-8ec4-5656cbedc02c had prompt '/review-code' and the child task was literally '/review-code'.
- cwd C:\github\Personal\TermAl, set explicitly: NOT resolved (delegation-da1b1881-29bc-4539-88f6-d3ef7940e736).
.claude/commands/review-code.md exists and is tracked in both the root and the worktree. Both reviewer sessions show agentCommandsRevision 0.

Impact: a Codex child gets the bare '/review-code' and has no slash-command mechanism to expand it, so the review contract is not delivered. Workaround used: pass the command body (without frontmatter) as the prompt.

Expected: resolution works for cwd = project root, as the tool description promises ('Single-line prompts matching a known slash command are resolved before spawning; cwd scopes command resolution'). Investigate the resolver's command lookup for the project root. A stale per-project command cache, keyed differently from the worktree cwd, is one hypothesis.
